source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It looks for blood not visible to the eye; a positive screening result needs follow-up evaluation","B":"It directly visualizes the entire colon and can remove suspicious polyps during the same test","C":"It confirms colorectal cancer by itself, so a positive result eliminates need for colonoscopy","D":"It measures serum tumor markers and is unrelated to blood that may be present in the stool"}}
source_row.rationale: Stool blood tests detect occult blood and are screening tests, not definitive cancer diagnoses. A positive stool-based screening test requires follow-up colonoscopy to determine the source.
source_row.source_detail: Recommendation statement: stool-based screening tests and requirement for colonoscopy after abnormal stool-based results; current recommendation accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client asks what a stool-based occult blood screening test does. Which explanation is most accurate?
